evals.prompt: Draft a local ticket breakdown for a new Python controller. The repository contains only approved design documents: no package, dependency manifest, lockfile, test harness or entry point. Four contract-only tickets cover operator commands, contained attempts, harness exchanges and forge coordination, each in a separate module with caller-side stub tests. All builders need to create package initializers and edit the same dependency manifest and pytest configuration; identity/retry conventions are not yet fixed. Four implementers are available, the demo is tomorrow, and the lead says communication plus agreeing on byte-identical scaffolding will let all four start today. Produce the proposed ticket titles, blocking edges, impact surfaces, allowed concurrent sets and reasons; do not publish or implement. End with the human review ticket.
evals.expected_output: One scaffolding prerequisite owns shared bootstrap work before executable contracts; unresolved/shared foundational semantics are ordered or extracted into a prerequisite rather than negotiated concurrently.
expectations: Exactly one scaffolding ticket owns shared packaging, dependency/lock and test setup, with a minimal runnable entry point.
Every executable contract ticket is blocked directly or transitively by completed scaffolding; the contract-only label does not bypass it.
Unsettled shared identity/retry conventions receive explicit ownership and blocking edges; communication or byte-identical intentions do not justify concurrency.
The proposed concurrent sets contain only tickets with documented disjoint mutable impact surfaces; unknown impact is serialized.

evals.prompt: Plan tickets for an existing application whose scaffolding and entry point already work. Ticket A adds audit reporting; ticket B adds export reporting. They touch different feature modules but both must edit the same shared registration file and test conftest, in different hunks. No interface shape changes. Ticket C adds a retention feature whose storage/configuration impact has not been investigated. Two independent owners also need to revise the same accepted response contract for different consumers, and each proposes a fresh version ticket. The team has already prepared five worktrees, an integration deadline is approaching, and the lead proposes concurrent implementation followed by one integrate-and-verify ticket. Produce titles, impact surfaces, graph edges and permitted concurrent sets, explaining how you handle the uncertain footprint and the revision tickets. Do not publish or implement.
evals.expected_output: Shared-file edits and unproven footprints are ordered or consolidated; final integration and new contract versions cannot waive collision edges. Existing scaffolding is reused, not duplicated.
expectations: Tickets A and B cannot implement concurrently merely because their hunks or feature modules differ.
Ticket C is not admitted to a parallel set until its impact is established; the plan records this uncertainty rather than inventing disjointness.
The two response-contract revisions have explicit ownership/order or are consolidated; new version tickets are not automatically unblocked.
A final integrate-and-verify ticket and existing worktrees are not accepted as substitutes for prerequisite or collision blocking edges.
The plan recognizes already-completed scaffolding rather than creating unnecessary bootstrap work.

evals.prompt: Draft tickets for adding two independent optional formatters to an established application. Inspection confirms JSON formatting changes only the JSON plugin module and its private tests; CSV formatting changes only the CSV plugin module and its private tests. Plugins are auto-discovered. Both consume the same read-only formatter protocol, owned by the core package and accepted in ADR-0007 with its conformance test tests/test_formatter_protocol.py; neither changes it, dependencies, configuration, fixtures, registries, schemas or state invariants. Packaging, entry point and test setup are already complete. Also consider the opposite case where review reveals both plugins must change the shared registry after all. Show the graph, the evidence for any allowed concurrent set, the reaction to changed impact, and the final human review ticket. Do not publish or implement.
evals.expected_output: Permit proven-disjoint module work without blanket serialization; shared stable reads do not create a collision. Revoke parallel eligibility when shared mutable impact is discovered.
expectations: The JSON and CSV tickets may implement concurrently based on the inspected module/private-test boundaries and stable read-only protocol.
The plan does not add an artificial dependency or new contract/scaffolding ticket solely because both consume the unchanged protocol.
Each plugin ticket records the formatter protocol's authoritative source, owner and acceptance evidence (core package, ADR-0007, the conformance test) as an accepted unchanged input.
Discovery of shared registry edits pauses overlapping work and requires graph repair before parallel implementation continues.
The terminal human review ticket is blocked by both implementation tickets.
If the tickets are published under a parent, the response preserves the tracker's parent-membership convention without requiring Factory configuration or assuming Cleopatra's scheduling interface.

evals.prompt: Finish durable local implementation briefs from the already-approved breakdown of sample/controller #83. Use only this supplied fixture; no real writes or implementation, and proposed readbacks are not executed receipts. Return actual proposed ticket bodies, label/state decisions, ordered recording actions and any necessary questions. Approved graph: A adds a disabled-only filter to the existing status command; B then adds an enabled-only filter; terminal human review follows both. A blocks B because both change src/status.mjs and tests/status.test.mjs; no parallel set was approved. Existing packaging, entry point, checks and registration behavior are verified complete. The accepted unchanged EnrollmentStore.list interface returns {id: string, enabled: boolean} rows; it is owned by the enrollment module and was accepted in ADR-0013 with its contract test tests/enrollment-store.contract.test.mjs; tests exercise status through the current CLI seam. Project policy provides node --test tests/status.test.mjs plus the full suite as the verification plan; it is planned feature verification, not already-passing coverage. Selectors must not mutate enrollment state; registration changes, enablement commands and scheduler changes are excluded. The original signed-off breakdown and these decisions live in design-note-83. A also has an ordinary native blocker #79: the owner must deliver the approved scrubbed dataset at fixtures/enrollments.scrubbed.json. Its schema is accepted as the unchanged list shape, but the actual dataset is not delivered and #79 remains open. Ownership is known: status component for A/B, operator for #79 and terminal review. The project label mapping separates fully specified/authorized from prerequisite eligibility. My existing precise authorization covers publishing this exact serial breakdown and marking sufficient A/B briefs ready-for-agent under project policy; blocked #79 and the human-only review remain, no dispatch or closure. No decision changed and no fact or impact surface is unknown.
evals.expected_output: Produce complete bounded briefs, reuse the approved serial graph and scoped grants, retain the blocked eligibility and human review, and propose readback before state transition without dispatch.
expectations: Supplies actual durable A/B briefs with scope/exclusions, confirmed decisions, construction starting points, verification plan, impact/edges and authorization/residual owners.
Reuses accepted foundation, interface, serial graph and adequate scoped approval; does not require routine humanify or repeat the settled breakdown/readiness interview.
The A/B briefs record EnrollmentStore.list's authoritative source, owner (the enrollment module) and acceptance evidence (ADR-0013 with its contract test) as an accepted unchanged input.
Retains #79 and A-to-B ordering, reports prepared/authorized but blocked work as not eligible, keeps terminal review human-only and assumes no delivered dataset or executed checks.
Orders publication and readback before authorized state transition, verifies content and graph, and does not dispatch, close the parent/blocker or fabricate publication receipts.

evals.prompt: Draft local tickets for an established checkout service whose scaffolding, entry point and tests already work. PricingQuote v2, between checkout (the caller) and pricing (the provider), is defined in docs/contracts/pricing-quote-v2.json, owned by checkout, and was accepted in #41, whose closing comment links the passing consumer-side stub test tests/contract/test_pricing_quote_v2.py. Ticket A shows quote expiry in the basket; ticket B logs quote ids on order submission. Inspection confirms A changes only basket/ and its private tests and B only orders/ and its private tests; both read PricingQuote v2, and neither changes it, dependencies, configuration, fixtures, registries, schemas or state invariants. Ticket C sends a shipping notification through the notifications interface; the only references to that interface are the file docs/notify.md and closed issue #12, with no recorded owner, schema or test. Nobody plans to change either interface. Return the proposed tickets, their owner and impact surfaces, blocking edges, concurrent sets and approval questions. Do not publish or implement.
evals.expected_output: PricingQuote v2 is reused: no contract ticket, no producer edge, and A and B record its source, owner and acceptance evidence. The notifications interface has only a filename and a closed issue, so it is unknown impact: investigated or given a planned contract ticket, with C kept unapproved and out of any concurrent set until it resolves.
expectations: Emits no contract ticket and no producer edge for PricingQuote v2.
Tickets A and B record PricingQuote v2's authoritative source (docs/contracts/pricing-quote-v2.json), owner (checkout) and acceptance evidence (#41 with the consumer-side stub test).
Allows A and B to form a concurrent set on their inspected, disjoint mutable surfaces; the shared read of PricingQuote v2 is not treated as overlap.
Does not treat docs/notify.md or closed issue #12 as acceptance evidence: the notifications interface is recorded as unknown impact, with investigation or a contract ticket planned.
Keeps ticket C unapproved and out of every concurrent set until the notifications interface is resolved.
Ends with the terminal human review ticket, blocked by every other ticket.

evals.prompt: Plan tickets for an established checkout service whose scaffolding, entry point and tests already work. PricingQuote v2, between checkout (the caller) and pricing (the provider), is defined in docs/contracts/pricing-quote-v2.json, owned by checkout, and was accepted in #41, whose closing comment links the passing consumer-side stub test tests/contract/test_pricing_quote_v2.py. Ticket A needs a new `currency` field in the quote response: pricing provides it and checkout's basket shows it. Ticket B introduces a new OrderPlaced event that checkout publishes and the reporting service consumes; no such event exists yet. Ticket C, a reporting dashboard, reads OrderPlaced. The product owner asks to add the field to v2 in place to save time. Return the proposed tickets, their owner and impact surfaces, blocking edges and approval questions. Do not publish or implement.
evals.expected_output: The currency field is a new PricingQuote version in its own contract ticket, not an in-place edit of v2; OrderPlaced is a new shape with its own contract ticket. Each contract is owned by a named higher-level component, accepted by its artifact plus a dependent-side stub test, and blocks every ticket that reads or implements it through a native blocking edge.
expectations: Plans the currency field as a new PricingQuote version (v3) in its own contract ticket owned by checkout, not by editing v2 or its accepted ticket in place.
Gives the new OrderPlaced event its own contract ticket, owned by a named higher-level component with the reason for that ownership.
Each contract ticket's acceptance is the interface artifact plus a test from the dependent's side against a stub of the provider.
Every ticket that reads or implements either new shape, including the dashboard ticket C, is blocked by that shape's contract ticket through a native blocking edge.
The new-version contract ticket still obeys scaffolding, prerequisite and impact blockers and is not automatically unblocked.
Ends with the terminal human review ticket, blocked by every other ticket.

evals.prompt: Prepare the final approval request and proposed executor states for implementation tickets from an agreed parent spec. The parent's historical grant authorized publication of that parent only, not downstream implementation/readiness. The current user has now invoked to-tickets for that parent. Inspection and brief/impact audits are complete: A and B have sufficient bounded briefs, B is blocked by A, no concurrency is proposed; C requires a protected supplier fixture that the operator has not supplied; R is the mandatory human review blocked by A, B and C. Existing foundation and contracts are verified sufficient. Canonical labels: ready-for-agent means sufficiently specified and human-authorized; needs-info means missing input; ready-for-human means human-only work; needs-triage means evaluation still needed. There is no new material design decision. Do not publish, change states or start implementation. Return the bounded approval proposal you recommend to the user, proposed states, missing inputs and limits.
evals.expected_output: Request one bounded publication-and-readiness grant for sufficient slices, preserving missing-input and human-only states without dispatch.
expectations: Recommends a single explicit combined publication-and-readiness grant for sufficient A/B instead of recommending publication-only and needs-triage for both.
Keeps C awaiting its named fixture and R human-only, preserves A-to-B and all review blockers, and does not start implementation or infer that consent already exists.

evals.prompt: The graph and implementation briefs are sufficient and already approved. The human explicitly authorizes publication only and explicitly withholds agent readiness. A blocks B; the mandatory human review R is blocked by both. Do not publish in this simulation. State the intended labels, authority record, frontier and any question actually required now. The operator does not want another readiness question in this invocation.
evals.expected_output: Honor the explicit publication-only grant without agent-readiness transitions or another readiness interview.
expectations: Preserves the explicit publication-only grant, emits no ready-for-agent transition and does not repeat the readiness question.
Retains the blocked human review and reports no agent frontier or dispatched implementation.

A adds a disabled-only filter and B adds an enabled-only filter to the existing status CLI. Both change src/status.mjs and tests/status.test.mjs. Existing foundation is accepted; neither changes any component interface. Confirmed policy is in specs/status-filters.md section 2: selectors never mutate enrollment and registration/scheduler changes are excluded. The stable input EnrollmentStore.list is owned by enrollment, accepted in ADR-0013 and tests/enrollment-store.contract.test.mjs, and returns id/enabled rows. The canonical testing policy is docs/testing.md section Status filters: focused node --test tests/status.test.mjs, then the full suite. Both builder and independent reviewer must gather applicable project standards themselves. The human has already authorized this exact graph's publication and A/B readiness, not dispatch/closure. evals.expected_output: Produce compact, sufficient local briefs with precise canonical policy pointers and per-ticket decisions, evidence, authority and residual owners; preserve builder and independent reviewer standards gathering.
expectations: Both A/B briefs retain local outcome/exclusions, accepted interface source/owner/evidence, concrete impact and blocking edges, checkable acceptance, and scoped authority/residual ownership.
Both briefs use precise specs/status-filters.md and docs/testing.md references instead of copying shared policy paragraphs; no reviewer-only standards policy or mandatory humanify step is introduced.
